messages:
Anya: Heads-up — found a community model 'hydrangea-9b' that a partner asked us to evaluate: https://huggingface.co/org/hydrangea/hydrangea-9b. License includes a custom addendum (Apache-2.0 + NonCommercialAddendum). Planning initial quantization/latency bench. Is this OK to onboard for internal experiments?
Miguel: Do we have provenance/weights origin? Any third-party checkpoints referenced in the README? Quick triage first.
Anya: README points to a weights repo and an addendum file: https://huggingface.co/org/hydrangea/NonCommercialAddendum.md — key line: 
```
"This model may not be used for commercial purposes or hosted as a paid API. Derivative models intended for commercial deployment are prohibited."
```
Samir: FYI this looks like a blocking clause for Hosted API and any pay-for-use offering. Private on-prem may be allowed depending on wording. I'll do a deeper license read but flagging: hosted = no, dedicated = contractual/edge case, private = probably ok. Paste the exact clause here when you have it.
Liz: From eval/quant side we can still do local experiments and benchmarks as long as we don't expose it via Hosted. Please tag the model as NC in the catalog if we proceed.
Anya: Proposed onboarding steps: 
- legal sign-off + clear deployability matrix
- provenance check (weights origin + commit history)
- quant smoke (q4_0 / q4_k_m / int8) on dev rig, record perplexity/regression
- offline evals (internal eval sets + safety checks)
- block routing to hosted/dedicated until cleared
Miguel: +1 to that order. I'll run the provenance check today and link results. Avoid any distributed benchmarking until legal confirms.
legal-bot: New ticket created: LEGAL-3245 - Hydrangea-9B license review. Assignee: Samir. ETA: 2 business days.
Samir: Thanks. Also need export-control check — does training data or weight origin trigger any EAR/ITAR concerns? Ops, can you run a quick country/party scan on the repo metadata?
ops-bot: Export-control scan completed. No flagged entities found in training-data metadata. Weights hosted from EU storage. Recommend formal classification if we intend to distribute internationally.
Liz: For quant experiments I'll prepare a short smoke plan (small eval set, mx batch sizes, measure latency + tok/sec). Will log experiment IDs here and include baseline (fp16) vs q4_0/q4_k_m/int8. If legal says NC absolute, we'll keep experiments internal and add a catalog flag: "license_non_commercial": true.
Anya: I'll update the intake sheet with fields: license_text_link, license_tags=["nc:no-hosting", "no-commercial"], provenance_link, legal_ticket=LEGAL-3245. Also adding a note to block automated model routing rules.
Miguel: Thanks — please do not push to staging/infrastructure that would make it externally reachable until we have explicit legal clearance. If legal allows limited customer trials we will require NDA + special contract terms.
Samir: Understood. I will prioritize the review and post a short decision summary here (allowed uses, hosting prohibition, derivative rule, export constraints). Follow-up in this thread after LEGAL-3245 lands.
Anya: Cool. I'll wait on the legal summary before kicking off distributed perf runs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
